Get started with nglscenes

Source: vignettes/nglscenes.Rmd
nglscenes.Rmd

Neuroglancer keeps everything it shows (layers, selected segments, camera position, layout and so on) in a JSON state, usually encoded in the URL. nglscenes reads, builds and edits these states from R.

library(nglscenes)

Scenes and layers are lists

A scene is the neuroglancer state as a named list with class ngs_scene, and each layer is the layer’s state with a class such as ngs_segmentation_layer. You can read and set fields with $ and [[ like with any other list:

sc <- ngs_scene(
  ngs_image_layer("precomputed://gs://neuroglancer-fafb-data/fafb_v14/fafb_v14_clahe",
                  name = "em"),
  ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://fafb-ffn1-20200412/segmentation",
                         name = "ffn1", segments = c(710435991, 2803641208)),
  layout = "3d"
)
sc
#> <ngs_scene> 2 layers: 1 image, 1 segmentation
#> Base URL: https://neuroglancer-demo.appspot.com/
#> 1: <image layer> "em" precomputed://gs://neurogla...ata/fafb_v14/fafb_v14_clahe
#> 2: <segmentation layer> "ffn1" precomputed://gs...412/segmentation (2 segments)

sc$layout
#> [1] "3d"
sc$layout <- "xy-3d"
sc$position <- c(109357, 41309, 5417)

All functions return a modified copy rather than changing the scene in place, so they work well with pipes.

Writing scenes

ngs_url() encodes the state in a URL for the scene’s neuroglancer instance:

url <- ngs_url(sc)
substr(url, 1, 120)
#> [1] "https://neuroglancer-demo.appspot.com/#!%7B%22layers%22%3A%5B%7B%22blend%22%3A%22default%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22em%22%2C%2"

ngs_open() opens that URL in the browser, ngs_to_clipboard() copies it, and ngs_to_json() / ngs_to_file() give you the JSON instead.

To use a different neuroglancer instance, change the base URL:

ngs_base_url(sc) <- "https://spelunker.cave-explorer.org/"
substr(ngs_url(sc), 1, 60)
#> [1] "https://spelunker.cave-explorer.org/#!%7B%22layers%22%3A%5B%"

Reading scenes

Scenes can be read from URLs (ngs_from_url()), JSON strings or state lists (ngs_from_string(), ngs_from_list()), files (ngs_from_file()) and the clipboard (ngs_from_clipboard()). URLs that point to a state server (?json_url=..., #!gs://..., #!middleauth+https://...) are fetched automatically.

sc2 <- ngs_from_url(url)
sc2
#> <ngs_scene> 2 layers: 1 image, 1 segmentation
#> Base URL: https://neuroglancer-demo.appspot.com/
#> 1: <image layer> "em" precomputed://gs://neurogla...ata/fafb_v14/fafb_v14_clahe
#> 2: <segmentation layer> "ffn1" precomputed://gs...412/segmentation (2 segments)

Parsed scenes round-trip unchanged: writing a scene you have read gives the same state back, including fields nglscenes doesn’t know about.

identical(ngs_to_json(sc2), ngs_to_json(ngs_from_url(ngs_url(sc2))))
#> [1] TRUE

Managing layers

Layers are referred to by name or by (1-based) position:

ngs_layer_names(sc)
#> [1] "em"   "ffn1"

sc <- sc |>
  ngs_add_layers(ngs_annotation_layer(name = "points")) |>
  ngs_move_layer("points", 1)
ngs_layer_names(sc)
#> [1] "points" "em"     "ffn1"

ngs_layer(sc, "em")$visible <- FALSE
sc <- ngs_drop_layer(sc, "points")

Layer names must be unique within a scene: adding a layer whose name is taken adds a suffix (e.g. "ffn1-2").

Segments and colours

Segment IDs are 64-bit integers, which R can’t represent exactly as numbers. nglscenes therefore always stores them as character, and converts numbers (or bit64::integer64 values) when they are set:

ngs_segments(sc)
#> [1] "710435991"  "2803641208"

The helpers for segmentation layers accept a layer or a scene. With a scene, layer picks the layer, or can be left out if there is only one segmentation layer:

sc <- sc |>
  ngs_add_segments(c("2803641209", "2803641210")) |>
  ngs_color_by(c("KC", "PN", "PN", "KC"), palette = "Okabe-Ito")

unlist(ngs_layer(sc, "ffn1")$segmentColors)
#>  710435991 2803641208 2803641209 2803641210 
#>  "#000000"  "#e69f00"  "#e69f00"  "#000000"

ngs_set_colors() sets colours directly, from a single colour, one colour per segment or colours named by segment ID:

sc <- ngs_set_colors(sc, c("710435991" = "red"), layer = "ffn1")

Annotations 

an <- ngs_annotation_layer(name = "somata") |>
  ngs_add_points(data.frame(id = c("a", "b"),
                            x = c(1000, 2000), y = c(500, 600), z = c(10, 20)))
as.data.frame(an)
#>   id    x   y  z
#> 1  a 1000 500 10
#> 2  b 2000 600 20

Combining scenes

+ adds all layers of the second scene to the first, and | merges layers that share a source (e.g. combines the segments of two segmentation layers) and adds the rest:

a <- ngs_scene(ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://x/seg", segments = 1:2))
b <- ngs_scene(ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://x/seg", segments = 2:3))

length((a + b)$layers)
#> [1] 2
ngs_segments(a | b)
#> [1] "1" "2" "3"

Graphene (CAVE) layers

Mainline neuroglancer and Spelunker spell CAVE chunkedgraph layers differently from the Seung-lab fork (e.g. ngl.flywire.ai), and each refuses the other’s spelling. ngs_for_viewer() converts all graphene layers in a scene:

fw <- ngs_scene(ngs_flywire_layer(segments = "720575940621039145"))
fw$layers[[1]]$type
#> [1] "segmentation"

fw2 <- ngs_for_viewer(fw, "seunglab")
fw2$layers[[1]]$type
#> [1] "segmentation_with_graph"
fw2$layers[[1]]$source
#> [1] "graphene://https://prod.flywire-daf.com/segmentation/1.0/fly_v31"

Fetching scenes from CAVE state servers requires a token, see ?ngs_cave_token.

Segment properties

Segment properties add labels and searchable tags to segments. Create them from a data frame and write them to an info file next to your segmentation:

props <- ngs_properties_from_df(data.frame(
  id = c(1, 2, 3),
  name = c("DA1_lPN", "DA1_lPN", "KCg-m"),
  class = factor(c("PN", "PN", "KC")),
  size = c(10.5, 12, 3)
))
props
#> <ngs_segment_properties> 3 segments, 3 properties
#>   name (label)
#>   class (tags)
#>   size (number)
ngs_write_info(props, "segment_properties/info")
